title: Fee check labels an extrapolated projection as the 'Verified saving a month' and hides its basis
label: bug
steps: As admin on a site with a few priced days in the current billing month (e.g. 3 confirmed days claiming Rs 5,000 each), open /sites/:id/savings. Read the Fee check card.
expected: The card shows a saving that was actually verified in the period, says it is the smaller of the two baselines, and, if any scaling to a month is done, says so beside the figure (plan 9.7: every money figure with its method; plan 8.4: never over-claim).
actual: verify.summary scales the claimed rupees per scored day to the whole billing month (`c / n * dim + mdi_c`, line 1113), takes the smaller baseline and averages months, then labels it `verified_saving_rs_per_month`. The FeeCard (fee-card.tsx lines 40-43) prints it as 'Verified saving a month' with the subtitle 'claimed against the native settings, per month in the period' (wrong on both counts: it is the min of native and tuned, and it is extrapolated) and never shows `fee.basis`. The verdict badge 'Fee within one third of the verified saving' can therefore be green on three days of data.
evidence: verify.py 1105-1119 (`basis` string documents the scaling but is only in the JSON); frontend/src/features/savings/fee-card.tsx 37-43 reads `fee.fee_rs_per_month`, `fee.verified_saving_rs_per_month`, `fee.within_one_third` only; `Savings['fee']` type (types/api.ts 816) has no `basis`.

title: Headline 'Saving against the native settings' is the all-days sum, including days that claim nothing
label: spec-mismatch
area: Savings / KPI tiles, ledger, monthly PDF
steps: Open /sites/:id/savings as admin at an advisory site where several days are 'Not applied', 'Awaiting confirmation' or 'Claim withheld'. Compare the big figure of the first tile with the small 'Claimed on verified days' line; do the same for the ledger's bold 'Saving, all days' row and the PDF headline.
expected: The headline money figure is the claim (plan 8.4: a 'not applied' day claims nothing; fidelity gates), with the unclaimed all-days figure, if shown at all, subordinate and explained; R8 2.12's headline ledger is the saving the product stands behind.
actual: verify.summary sums `d['saving_rs']` over every day regardless of fidelity or withheld claim (line 1053) and adds the month MDI lever (1078); savings-kpis.tsx puts that `saving_rs` in the tile's large value with `claimed_rs` as a subtitle; savings-ledger.tsx 76-85 bolds 'Saving, all days' and shows 'Claimed' as a plain row; reports.py 115-119 prints 'Saving' before 'Claimed (applied days)'. At a monitor-tier site (the demo mall) the headline is the noise of actual-vs-native replay presented as a saving.
evidence: verify.py 1050-1053, 1078; savings-kpis.tsx 32-33; savings-ledger.tsx 76-85; reports.py 115-119; fleet route also exposes both (routes_savings.py 203).

title: MDI lever is computed from month-to-date peaks on the default 'This month' period and claimed whole on a single claiming day, with no 'full-month counterfactual' label
label: spec-mismatch
steps: Mid-month, open /sites/:id/savings (default period 'This month') at an MDI-billed site (B-2/B-3). Read the 'Maximum demand (MDI)' lever row and the tile headline; then confirm one day's table applied and recompute.
expected: Plan 8.2: MDI is the month's single highest block, so the lever comes 'from the full-month counterfactual only, labelled as such'; a partial month's MDI difference is provisional and should be marked, and a month's MDI lever should not be claimed on the strength of one claiming day.
actual: `mdi_by_month` uses the max peaks of whatever days fall in the period (lines 1061-1073), adds it to `saving_rs` for every month touched, and adds it to `claimed_rs` whenever `months[k][3] > 0`, i.e. one confirmed/partial day in the month (1075). The ledger row (levers.ts line 12) and the 'Maximum demand by month' list (savings-ledger.tsx 10-18) carry no provisional/partial-month mark. Period is calendar-month while MDI rows are keyed by billing month (`bill_month`), so with a `reading_day` connection the listed month key can span outside the chosen period.
evidence: verify.py 1061-1078; levers.ts 12; savings-ledger.tsx 101-105; period.ts 22-31 (no billing-period option).

title: PUT /sites/:id/pilot stores the body unvalidated and lets the client overwrite the sign-off record and the amendment history
label: bug
steps: As admin, after POST /pilot/start, send PUT /api/sites/:id/pilot with {"signoff": {"by": "someone else", "at": "2026-01-01", "name": "X"}, "amendments": []} or {"criteria": "abc", "baseline_days": -5}.
expected: A strict request model (HANDOFF section 4: request models forbid unknown fields) accepting only baseline_start/baseline_days/criteria with types and ranges; `signoff` and `amendments` are server-owned and never writable; a started pilot's amendment trail cannot be erased (R8 2.13: 'pre-register the pilot so the saving cannot be argued about afterwards').
actual: `data = {**cur['pilot'], **{k: v for k, v in inp.items() if k in PILOT_DEFAULT}}` accepts `signoff` and `amendments` because both are keys of PILOT_DEFAULT (lines 131-133, 150), and stores any JSON for `criteria`/`baseline_days`/`baseline_start` without checking; the page then crashes on `p.pilot.criteria[c.key]` (criteria-tab.tsx 27) if criteria is not an object. The amendment appended at line 152 is itself replaced by the client's `amendments` in the same merge order (client value wins, then line 152 appends to the client's list).
evidence: routes_savings.py 131-133, 145-156; no pydantic model; frontend criteria-tab.tsx 26-27 assumes an object.

title: Switchback figures silently include the carry-over credit; the credit is never shown and the 'unadjusted' subtitle is wrong
label: spec-mismatch
steps: At a site with a painted calendar and 6+ priced days per arm, open /sites/:id/savings?view=switchback and read the two 'Saving per day' tiles and their subtitles.
expected: Plan 8.2: 'Carry-over is priced, not removed ... the report shows the credit beside the saving'; the subtitle should describe what the number is; the 15 %/Rs 300-a-day agreement check between counterfactual and switchback (plan 8.2, tracker VER-08) should be shown.
actual: verify.switchback_result adds `per_day` carry-over to both `saving_rs_per_day_unadjusted` and `_adjusted` (lines 1225-1227) and returns `carry_over_credit_rs`, `carry_over_rs_per_plan_day`, `*_before_carry_over` and `carry_over_credits[]`; the frontend `Switchback` type (types/api.ts 850-854) omits all of them and the panel prints 'mean native-day cost less mean plan-day cost' for a figure that is not that. No agreement statistic exists anywhere.

title: Savings CSV and the report CSV lack the tariff version, capture version and claim columns; the PDF says the CSV annex dates the tariff versions
label: spec-mismatch

actual: routes_savings.savings_csv writes day, saving_native_rs, saving_tuned_rs, fidelity, costs, litres, peak only: no claimed_rs, no claim_withheld, no plan id, no tariff or capture version. reports.py 142-155 adds plan_ids but neither version nor claim columns, while the PDF footer (line 159) states 'tariff versions as dated in the CSV annex'. Summing the saving column counts not-applied, pending, native-block and withheld days.

title: Monthly savings report covers a fraction of plan 8.5; no company roll-up or pilot report although the tracker marks VER-10 done
label: feature-gap

Tracker EMS_BUILD_PROGRESS.md line 174 marks VER-10 [x] including 'per company' and 'the pilot write-up template'.
actual: The PDF has: headline table, ledger against native only (not tuned), method sentence, an energy table, daily rows. No switchback section, no carry-over credits, no bill comparison, no KPI grid (MDI by month, reserve adequacy, forecast skill, control health), no assumptions/GST note, no tuned ledger, no company roll-up, no pilot report kind (KINDS line 24 has three kinds), no tier-specific title. Report 'preliminary' sentence omits the switchback-weeks condition.

title: Monthly PDF prints 'Diesel saved 0 L' when the genset was unmetered, and prints a saving for days whose claim is withheld without any mark
label: bug
steps: At a site whose genset has no fuel signal for the whole month (every day `genset_unknown`, levers.genset null), generate the Monthly savings report; also include a day with `claim_withheld: import_unknown`.
expected: 'not metered' (as the web ledger says, savings-ledger.tsx 56) rather than a zero; a withheld day marked in the daily rows (plan 8.4 never over-claim; DESIGN_LOG round 3/4 withheld days claim nothing).
actual: verify.summary stores `litres_saved: round(litres, 1)` summing `or 0.0` (line 1055, 1079), never null, and reports.py line 117 prints it with ' L'; the daily rows (146-148) print `saving_native_rs` and `fidelity` only, so a withheld day shows a rupee figure with 'confirmed' beside it and no withheld mark; the CSV has no claim_withheld column either.

title: Bills can only be entered and rebuilt for the site's first connection
label: feature-gap
steps: On a site with two grid connections (plan 9.6: the Karachi feed mill, 'two connections, the MDI line on two bills'), open Savings > Bill comparison > Enter a bill. Try to enter the second connection's bill.
expected: Plan 8.2 layer 3: 'the DISCO bill per connection and settlement period'; the dialog lets the person pick the connection and the list says which connection each bill belongs to.
actual: add_bill uses `conns[0]` for the rebuild and stores `conns[0]['id']` (lines 1248-1270); the dialog (bill-dialog.tsx) has no connection field and the BillCard (bills-panel.tsx 52-59) never shows `connection_id`. The second connection's bill is rebuilt against the first connection's tariff and meter series.

title: Bill comparison collects peak/off-peak units and MDI but never compares them line by line; only the total is checked, and no baseline-arm bill is rebuilt
label: feature-gap
steps: Enter a bill with Peak units, Off-peak units and MDI filled in; open the bill card.
expected: R8 2.12 Bill comparison: 'the DISCO bill as entered or uploaded vs the rebuilt bill for both arms, line by line: units by window, MDI kW and charge, adders, net-billing credit, GST'; plan 6.3 step 13: every line's residual logged.
actual: BillCard reads only `real.total_rs`, `real.reference` and `real.previous_reading_date`; the typed units_peak, units_off_peak and mdi_kw (stored in `real`, verify.py 1262) are never shown or diffed against the rebuilt energy and demand lines; only the rebuilt (actual) arm's bill is produced (rebuild_bill, verify.py 1278), no native-arm bill.

actual: Neither calendar-tab.tsx, routes_savings.switchback_paint (80-94) nor pilot_start (159-174) look at the tier; verify.compute_day labels every monitor day `recommendation_only` (lines 717-718) yet switchback_result (1190-1230) still regresses 'plan' days against 'native' days, so a monitor site can show a 'Saving per day' that compares native settings with native settings. The Savings ledger title is fixed ('Ledger by lever', savings-ledger.tsx 58) and the Switchback tab's empty state invites painting the calendar at any tier.

title: Pilot success criteria are stored but never scored, and the genset and cycling gates are missing
label: feature-gap
steps: Set criteria in tab D and start the pilot; look anywhere (Savings, Reports, Pilot review) for the criteria compared with the measured result after some weeks.
expected: R8 2.13 tab D: gates prefilled (saving ≥ 3× fee, genset run-hours down ≥ 15 % at genset sites, ≥ 90 % of outages covered without deeper cycling than baseline), 'the genset gate hidden without a genset'; plan 8.5: the pilot write-up 'with the pre-registered success and kill criteria of Part 15.3 filled in'.

Backend has no reject/withdraw, diff or per-site simulate route (routes_tariffs.py). Tracker UI-03 [~]; HANDOFF 8.C lists it.

title: Alert rule set covers a fraction of the plan's categories; no Savings, Product, Genset-condition, edge/plan-expiry, data-gap or bill-residual alerts exist
label: feature-gap
steps: Read alerts.evaluate and alerts.nightly; compare with R8 2.16's category list and plan 9.3 UI-16. Filter the inbox by category Savings or Product.
expected: Data (stale, gap > 1 h, clock drift, CSV import failed), Control (read-back mismatch, write budget, local override, fallback, edge offline, plan expired, infeasible), Reserve (incl. outage not covered), Battery, Genset (unrequested start, below minimum load, fuel low, request not acted on), Forecast (bust, feed down, stage change), Tariff (regime expiry, SRO notice, bill rebuild > 2 %), Savings (negative saving day, unconfirmed apply), Product.

title: Switchback carry-over is priced at plan-to-native boundaries only
label: spec-mismatch
steps: Read _carry_over_credits; paint a calendar and inspect `carry_over_credits` in GET /switchback: only boundaries where a plan block precedes a native block appear.
expected: Plan 8.2: 'at every block boundary the bill engine credits the arm that ends with more stored energy by (E_end_A - E_end_B) x v_end'.
actual: Native-to-plan boundaries carry no credit (docstring 1160-1162: no plan replay on a native day). The plan block therefore starts with whatever the native block left, unpriced; the direction of any bias depends on the site, so this is a known asymmetry rather than a proven over-claim. The per-day ledger's carry_over lever is separate and unaffected.

title: Switchback calendar never puts a live site on its native arm: the tick keeps publishing the plan on native-block days
label: spec-mismatch
steps: 1. Paint a calendar (PUT /api/sites/{id}/switchback) and start the pilot (POST /pilot/start) so blocks are locked. 2. On a day whose block arm is 'native', call GET /api/sites/{id}/plan and, with the site key, GET /api/sites/{id}/plans/current/message. 3. Read verify.arm_on callers: grep shows it is used only by demo.py:162 (_policy_for, the twin history). plans.tick (plans.py:391-470) decides 'held' only from control_release (plans.py:140-150), which reads pause_control/force_native overrides; nothing creates one from the calendar. compute_day only labels the day (verify.py:711-716 'native_block').
expected: Brief, Pilot design phase 2: 'Days randomly assigned to baseline or optimiser' - on a native block the inverter runs its own settings (closed loop: the edge gets a release message as for force_native; advisory: the operator is told not to key a table). Tracker VER-08: 'the arm applied to the plan (a baseline block plans native)'.
actual: On a native-block day the tick stores an 'active' plan, the edge pulls a signed plan message (plans.signed_message, plans.py:694-712), advisory sites still raise apply_unconfirmed (alerts._peak_unconfirmed), and the ledger merely stamps the day fidelity='native_block' and claims nothing. switchback_result (verify.py:1190-1233) then regresses 'native' days that in fact ran the plan against plan days, so the measured increment (and the kill decision built on it) is meaningless. Only the demo twin honours the arm, so the demo looks right while a real pilot would not.
evidence: plans.py:140-150 control_release reads only ('pause_control','force_native'); plans.py:391-470 tick has no switchback lookup; grep 'arm_on|switchback' in plans.py/routes_plans.py/sites.py returns nothing; demo.py:161-178 _policy_for is the only consumer of verify.arm_on; verify.py:1125-1157 plan_switchback/arm_on only write and read the table.

title: Pilot success/kill criteria are stored and displayed but never evaluated against the measured KPIs
label: feature-gap
steps: 1. Read PILOT_DEFAULT.criteria (routes_savings.py:131-133: min_saving_pct, max_unserved_kwh, reserve_adequacy_pct, fidelity_pct, fee_multiple, forecast_pv_nrmse_max). 2. grep those keys across backend/gridlytics and frontend/src: they appear only in routes_savings.py (storage), frontend/src/features/pilot/criteria-tab.tsx (editing) and review-tab.tsx:84-87 (listing). 3. No route, nightly job, report or page computes pass/fail; VER-07 (offline backtest and go/no-go template) is '[ ]'.
expected: Brief 'Success and kill criteria': success at 2 of 3 sites when the verified increment over the tuned baseline is >= 3x the fee with zero optimiser-caused unserved critical load; kill if the increment is below the fee after 8 weeks of switchback; deep review: '>=90% of outages covered', '>=15% run-hour reduction at genset sites'. The product should state, per site and per gate, pass/fail from its own ledger.

title: One MDI rate (the last scored day's) prices every month's MDI lever; wrong across tariff versions and Tariff F seasons
label: bug
steps: 1) summary() loops over all days of the period and keeps a single `rate = d.get('mdi_rate') or rate` (1069), then prices every month with it: `mdi_by_month = {k: (...) * rate ...}` (1073). 2) Each day's `mdi_rate` already carries its month's factor: tariffs.vectors 754 `rate_rs_per_kw = fixed x fixed_factor x _seasonal_factor(month)`, and `_seasonal_factor` is the multiplier in season and 0.0 outside it (tariffs.py:490-495). 3) Request a period at a seasonal (season_months) connection spanning an off-season month followed by an in-season month, or a period across an approved tariff change.
expected: Each month's MDI lever priced at that month's own rate (the per-day row already stores it).
actual: The last day's rate is applied to all months: an off-season month gets charged the in-season rate (over-claim), or in the reverse order the in-season month's MDI lever is zeroed; a tariff change mid-period misprices the earlier month.
evidence: verify.py:1045, 1069, 1073; tariffs.py:490-495, 752-755; compute_day stores `mdi_rate` per day (754).

title: Headline 'Saving', the ledger by lever, the daily bars and both CSVs include withheld days' partial levers and non-claiming days; CSVs carry no claimed/withheld column
label: ux
steps: 1) compute_day 736-742: on an `import_unknown` day the grid levers are None but genset, wear and carry_over are still summed into `saving_rs`; on a `battery_flow_unknown` day the grid and genset levers are summed. summary 1050-1053, 1078 adds every day's levers and `saving_rs` regardless of fidelity (not_applied, native_block, recommendation_only) or `claim_withheld`. 2) Frontend: the first KPI tile shows `native.saving_rs` as 'Saving against the native settings' (savings-kpis.tsx:32-33, claimed only in the sub-line); the ledger table's levers and 'Saving, all days' (savings-ledger.tsx:69-80) and the bars (daily-savings-chart.tsx:14) use the same figures. 3) Exports: routes_savings.savings_csv header (routes_savings.py:66-69) and the report CSV (reports.py:142-155) have `saving_native_rs` and `fidelity` but no `claimed_rs` or `claim_withheld`, so a withheld day exports as fidelity 'confirmed' with a rupee saving; the PDF daily rows (reports.py:146-148) likewise.
expected: Plan 8.4 'never over-claim' and 8.5 (CSV 'so a dispute can be re-run'): the largest number on the page and every exported row should be the claim or be unmistakably labelled; a withheld day should contribute nothing (or null) to any headline and carry its withheld reason in exports.
actual: A reader of the page or the CSV takes the unclaimed, partially-levered total as the saving; a day whose claim is withheld for an unknown import still adds a carry-over credit (energy possibly charged from the unmetered grid) to the headline.
evidence: verify.py:742, 1050-1053, 1078; savings-kpis.tsx:32-33; savings-ledger.tsx:69-80; daily-savings-chart.tsx:14; routes_savings.py:66-69; reports.py:115-125, 142-155.

title: CSV annexes lack the tariff version and capture version the plan requires, while the PDF says the tariff versions are 'dated in the CSV annex'
label: spec-mismatch
steps: 1) reports.generate writes the PDF footer 'Native capture version N; tariff versions as dated in the CSV annex' (159-160). 2) The report CSV header (142-143) is day, import_kwh, export_kwh, pv_kwh, load_kwh, genset_hours, litres, outage_minutes, peak_kw [, saving_native_rs, saving_tuned_rs, fidelity, plan_ids]: no tariff version, no capture version. 3) routes_savings.savings_csv (66-69) has neither plan ids nor versions.
expected: Plan 8.5 and VER-03: 'the data behind every figure downloadable as CSV with the tariff version, the capture version and the plan ids'; the day row already stores `native_capture_version` and `icp_case`.
actual: The PDF promises a column that does not exist; a dispute cannot be re-run from the export alone.

title: Off-grid per-day carry-over is noisy: the per-day ledger drifts from a continuous replay by thousands of rupees (known, open)
label: bug
steps: 1) compute_day prices the carry-over as `(e_end_actual - e_end_native) x v_end` (733) with `v_end = eta_d x c_next - wear` and, off-grid, `c_next` the genset's marginal cost at `night_load_ratio` (669-675, 610-627): Rs 172-184/kWh at the farm. 2) Both replays restart each day from the actual SoC, so the native arm is re-credited daily for energy the actual arm holds. 3) DESIGN_LOG round 5 'Open': paired 11-day farm rebuilds show the per-day ledger minus the continuous replay ranging -6.2k to +7.9k Rs, the carry-over lever 'swings by tens of thousands of rupees and largely offsets the genset lever'.
expected: HANDOFF 8.A.1 done-criterion: the per-day ledger tracks the continuous replay within about Rs 1k over 11 days on several seeds before any off-grid pilot; Part 8.2's carry-over is meant to be priced, not to dominate the ledger.
actual: Customers at an off-grid site see a per-day ledger whose sign on a given day is set by the carry-over valuation rather than by fuel burnt; monthly totals can be over- or under-stated by several thousand rupees per 11 days. Documented as open; not fixed.
evidence: verify.py:610-627, 669-675, 733; docs/DESIGN_LOG.md round 5 'Open: the per-day carry-over at off-grid sites is noisy'; HANDOFF.md §8.A.1.

title: Metering factor (VER-13) not fitted or applied: both arms and the bill rebuild use raw CT energy and MDI; no out-of-band factor is ever raised as a data finding
label: feature-gap
steps: 1) rebuild_bill calls `tariffs.rebuild(...)` without `energy_scalar`/`mdi_scalar` (verify.py:1278-1288; defaults 1.0 at tariffs.py:506-507). 2) price_arm (107-126) applies no factor to either arm. 3) The `bills` table stores real/rebuilt/difference_pct only (add_bill 1268-1270); nothing fits a factor from two bills or tests a third, and nothing flags a factor outside 0.97-1.03.
expected: Plan 6.3/8.2/8.4 and VER-13: one energy scalar and one MDI scalar per connection fitted on two bills, tested on a held-out third, applied to both arms before pricing; a factor outside 0.97-1.03 is a data finding; the 2% bill gate closes only when a held-out bill passes.
actual: A CT that under-reads against the DISCO register (a load the inverter does not see) scales every rupee lever and the MDI lever silently, and the bill comparison can never reach the gate. The bearable-basis half of VER-13 is in place (energy_factor, recovered_taxes_rs), the factor half is absent.
evidence: verify.py:1278-1288; tariffs.py:506-507, 536-544; EMS_BUILD_PROGRESS.md line 110 VER-13 `[ ]`; HANDOFF §8.C.

title: Days scored mid-month keep a projected ICP case and scaled month totals; nothing re-scores a month at its end, after late data, a new capture or an approved tariff/FCA version
label: feature-gap
steps: 1) `_minute_prices` (69-92) settles the ICP case from `month_totals(site_id, conn, day)` (38-57), which before the month ends scales the metered minutes to date up to the whole billing month. 2) scheduler.nightly_company (scheduler.py:38-53) scores only yesterday; no job re-runs compute_day for the month's earlier days when the month closes or when `native_for_day`, an adder (FCA) or a tariff version changes. 3) At an ICP site, days 1-20 score 'below' (TOU rates); the month ends 'above' (flat ICP rate on every kWh). Days 1-20 stay priced at TOU rates in the ledger, the report and the fee check unless an operator presses Recompute (routes_savings.py:46-56: synchronous, 62-day cap, 5 s MILP bound per day).
expected: Plan 8.2: the ICP lever 'comes from the full-month counterfactual only'; 8.4: every day re-scorable with the inputs of its day; the month's figures should settle automatically once the month (and its FCA) is known.
actual: The month's rupees depend on when each day was scored; a month that flips ICP case, or whose FCA is approved after the days were scored, shows stale per-day levers.

title: Carry-over credit only at plan-to-native boundaries; a native block that hands over a fuller battery is uncredited
label: spec-mismatch
steps: 1) `_carry_over_credits` (1159-1176) skips every pair unless `a.arm == 'plan' and b.arm == 'native'`. 2) At a backup-mode native (holds 90-100 % while the grid is up) a native block ends full; the next plan block's first day spends that energy with no debit. 3) switchback_result adds only plan-to-native credits to the plan's saving (1224-1227).
expected: Plan 8.2: 'at every block boundary the bill engine credits the arm that ends with more stored energy by (E_end_A - E_end_B) x v_end'. On a native block's last day the plan arm's end energy can be approximated from the native day's `baseline` replay versus the actual, or the native-to-plan hand-over priced at the measured E_end difference between the last native day and what the plan's first day inherits.
actual: Asymmetric accounting: with self-use natives it under-claims, with hold/backup natives it over-claims the plan block's first day. The docstring records the omission as a limit; DESIGN_LOG does not.

title: Switchback 'adjusted' saving is fitted with 5 coefficients on as few as 6 days and the 15 %/Rs 300 agreement check is absent
label: feature-gap
steps: 1) switchback_result returns a result once `len(y) >= 6` and both arms present (1216); the regression (1221) has an intercept, the arm, PV, load and outage hours: 5 parameters, so with 6-8 days the adjusted figure has one to three degrees of freedom and no uncertainty is reported. 2) No code compares the switchback saving with the counterfactual saving on the switchback levers (Part 8.2's 15 % or Rs 300/day rule; VER-08).
expected: A minimum sample well above the parameter count (or a confidence bound as Part 15.3's 'lower 80 percent confidence bound' needs) and the agreement statistic shown beside the two estimates.
actual: A noisy adjusted figure is shown as a KPI ('Saving per day, adjusted') from the sixth priced day; the counterfactual-versus-switchback disagreement that the plan calls 'a finding, not a rounding' is never computed.

title: Report wording: the Preliminary sentence omits two of the four conditions, and the baseline at manual-genset sites includes an assumed operator rule the capture does not record
label: ux
steps: 1) reports.py:109 prints 'Preliminary. Fewer than 28 verified days, the month is not over, or a fuel adjustment of the period is not yet billed.' while verify.summary (1099) also requires a native capture and 8 switchback weeks; the web page lists all four (savings-page.tsx:48-53). 2) reports.py:159-160 states 'Figures are measured against a replay of the inverter's own settings on the same day's sun, load and outages', but at a manual-start genset site the native arm also applies twin.simulate's operator rule 'someone starts it when the lights would go out and stops it once the battery is charged' (twin.py:396-397), which is not part of any capture. 3) The 'Ledger by lever' table (121-125) sums all days including unclaimed and withheld ones without saying so.
expected: Plan 8.2: 'At genset sites the operator's genset actions are logged per arm and the genset stream is reported with its fidelity rather than claimed as blinded'; 8.5: the method stated; a lawyer-reviewed claim wording is owner task O9.
actual: A CFO reading the PDF is told the baseline is purely the inverter's settings and is given an incomplete reason for 'Preliminary'.
